artwork_title: Original copper plate (Planche VI) from Carmen Portfolio, with its accompanying etching on paper (2 works)
material: copper plate, etching, engraving, letterpress, Montval paper
provenance: Galerie Michael, Beverly Hills, California | Richard Evenson, The Carmen Collection, Portland | Georgetown Frame Shop, Washington, D.C. | Acquired directly from the above by the present | | In 1948 Picasso worked on the copper plates that would illustrate the portfolio Carmen. He had moved to the beach town of Golfe-Juan with his young lover, Françoise Gilot, who had just given birth to their second child, Paloma. On May 30th, the day he started the project, he completed 9 etchings, including this one. He inscribed each copper plate with the location, date, title and page number. Although many of his etchings often had the date of completion inscribed into the plate, the inscriptions for Carmen were removed when the portfolio was editioned, probably not to interfere with Prosper Mérimée's accompanying text.
subject_matter: copper plate, etching, text, engraving, abstract lines, portfolio, page 34, cancellation marks, inscription, characters
